focus: Bug pass on /doctor:env, /doctor:update, /doctor:overlay, /doctor:install and /doctor:ci: exit codes, check-route writes, flag and positional mismatches, wrong-root resolution

graphEvents.label: Does /doctor:ci map every real failure to a distinct, documented exit code?
update check exit_policy has no slot for exit 1
ci-report exit 1 conflates parse failure with uncaught throw
/doctor:env route entry lacks allowed_flags and gate3_location

label: /doctor:update check documents only exit 0 and exit 2, but release-update.cjs exits 1 for every non-usage failure and writes the failure body as JSON on stdout, so an agent presenting the command output renders a parseable report-shaped object for a failed check
verify: node .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/release-update.cjs check --repo /tmp --json; echo $?  # exit 1 with {ok:false,error} on stdout

label: /doctor:ci --sha rejects uppercase hex with exit 2 while the route asset and _routes.yaml document a bare 40-hex placeholder, so a SHA copied from a GitHub page or log that renders mixed case is refused with the case constraint appearing only in the error text

/doctor:env silently drops 8 documented variables because ENV-REFERENCE.md carries a third table header (Variable | Set to | Read by) that matches neither supported shape, and .env.example mentions the SKILLED_LOOP_* family only in prose, so a selector naming SKILLED_LOOP_ID or SESSION_RELAUNCH_GOAL_PACKET hits the unmatched-selector error

/doctor:env is the only mutating route in this scope whose _routes.yaml entry declares neither allowed_flags (so its single documented flag --dry-run is invisible to the manifest) nor gate3_location (so the Gate-3 answer has no mutation target), while /doctor:ci report and /doctor:install declare both

/doctor:install's workflow promises three positional forms (list, ? and menu) that its route entry never declares, and the entry carries target: guide with no default_target, unlike /doctor:ci report which marks its report target default, so a bare /doctor:install depends on a defaulting rule it does not opt into

confidence: high on two roots / medium on frequency
label: /doctor:install resolves its two build probes against the agent's cwd (test -d .skilled/... and node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs) but its third probe against the script's own root (symlink-engine source defaults to SCRIPT_ROOT), so a run started inside a vendored target measures the target's builds and plans the checkout's links while the route still claims it checked one checkout
verify: cd /tmp && test -d .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/dist; echo $?  # 1, while 0 from the repo root

label: /doctor:ci report's asset maps exit 1 to one cause (a workflow failed to parse) but four report steps run outside a try, so any throw from readVariables, resolveNewestNonRebuildSha, parseWorkflows or loadWorkflows reaches Node's default exit 1 and the agent renders the parse-failure branch with no per-file line to show
overlay-engine.cjs status on a non-vendored tree exits 2 with a named missing manifest path, creates no .build-lock and writes no state directory, so the documented exit-2 mapping is accurate

release-update.cjs check --repo . --json exits 0 with status current, writes no state-log file (the doctor-update state directory still holds only README.md) and leaves git status --porcelain unchanged, so the check route's no-write claim holds

symlink-engine.cjs validates flags per command with a separate allowlist for check, plan, apply and unlink and requires --root for check, so /doctor:install's documented invocation matches the parser exactly and no flag mismatch exists there

skill-advisor.cjs list-tools --format json exits 0 and touched no file under .skilled/skills/.state/advisor within 90 seconds, but a pre-existing advisor daemon means this cannot prove the /doctor:install build check is write-free
specs/001-test-feature/ is still untracked in the working tree, left by an earlier iteration of this run; removal is outside this child's write authority and it was left in place

ci-report.cjs --help and symlink-engine.cjs --help both exit 2 with a UsageError while overlay-engine.cjs --help and release-update.cjs --help exit 0, so two of the four scripted routes in this scope cannot be probed by an operator who guesses --help

direction: A check-only doctor route performs a hidden write: overlay status, update check and symlink check were each run and left the tree, the state directories and git status untouched
reason: No write found in the four check or status modes exercised this iteration; the doctor-install advisor probe stays inconclusive because a daemon was already running

direction: A flag that /doctor:install passes is rejected by symlink-engine.cjs
reason: parseArgs builds a per-command allowlist at symlink-engine.cjs:156 and check accepts root, source, runtimes, include, linkInstructions and json, which is exactly what doctor-install.yaml step 3 passes

direction: ci-toggle.cjs swallows a refusal by exiting 0
reason: main returns plan.status === 'REFUSED' ? 1 : 0 at ci-toggle.cjs:334, so the refusal branch reaches the agent as exit 1 exactly as doctor-ci-toggle.yaml claims
